input.rationale: One limitation of the configuration-recovery account was that the empty-configuration case had only been observed on a single-voter prefix, leaving the multi-node consequence of a voter that can never participate argued rather than observed. This batch registers the fixed experiment that measures it in a three-voter group, with the same node and log restarted with the replay on and off.

scope.description: Three in-memory voters A, B and C. A leader is chosen, three commands are committed so A's staged commit index is non-zero, A is stopped and restarted over its own stores in one case with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and in the other with it disabled, and the harness records A's tracked configuration. The other two voters are then shut down, and the harness samples A's state every 5ms for 1500ms, reporting how often it was a follower, a candidate or a leader.
assumptions: The cluster configuration is stable, so no new configuration entry reaches A after its restart and its tracked configuration can only come from its own startup path.

A's stores hold no snapshot, so with the replay enabled the startup scan is skipped and A ends up with an empty tracked configuration; with the replay disabled the scan covers the log and A recovers the three-voter configuration.

Removing the other voters by shutting them down tests whether the surviving voter attempts candidacy, not whether it can win; with the recovered three-voter configuration A cannot win either, since its quorum is two.
The two cases use separate clusters built the same way, so the flag is the only difference.
excluded: No assertion about winning an election or about cluster availability; the observation is the candidate attempt itself.
No membership change after the restart, no partitioned-but-live peer, and no production store or process-level restart.

experiment.prefix: For each case the harness builds three assuranceMultiNode values (random in-memory transport addresses, inmemConfig with RestoreCommittedLogs true and a fresh MockFSM per node), wires the transports pairwise, calls BootstrapCluster with the same three-voter configuration on each and NewRaft for each. It waits for a real leader and commits three commands through it, then records A's staged commit index and shuts A down. A new transport bound to A's address is connected to B and C, and NewRaft is called on A's stores with a fresh MockFSM and the case's RestoreCommittedLogs value; the harness reads A's tracked configurations through r.configurationsCh and reports the latest index, the voter count and the member ids. It then shuts B and C down, samples A's state every 5ms for 1500ms, and reports the follower, candidate and leader sample counts together with the last snapshot index and the final state.
experiment.responsibility: raft's startup recovery is responsible for establishing the configuration the log already contains, and a voter's follower loop is responsible for attempting to acquire leadership when it stops hearing from a leader and its configuration allows it.

comparisons.description: A voter whose own log establishes the cluster configuration must attempt candidacy once it hears no leader and the other voters are gone; a violating witness shows a configured voter that can never become a candidate.

Control: the same node with the same log restarted with the replay disabled recovers its configuration and does attempt candidacy, which attributes the inertness in the companion case to the recovery path.

scope.description: Restart a single-voter raft node on top of its own retained stores, once with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and once with it disabled, on two prefix shapes: a prefix with no snapshot, and a prefix whose snapshot precedes a committed configuration change. Report the recovered configuration (index, membership) beside the newest configuration entry in the node's own log, and whether the restarted node reaches leadership inside a 1.5s window (30 election/heartbeat timeouts at 50ms).
assumptions: The prefix runs with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled so that the commit index is staged into the commit-tracking log store; otherwise a restart with the feature enabled reads 0 and the scan start would equal the snapshot index.
The restarted node keeps the same address and ID as the prefix, so the configuration recorded in its log and snapshot still refers to it.

The FSM is an in-memory MockFSM and a fresh instance is used for each restart, which is the mode the feature targets; the FSM state is therefore rebuilt from the snapshot plus the replayed committed logs.

InmemCommitTrackingStore is a test facility whose StageCommitIndex does not share a write with StoreLogs; the probe uses it only as the store that exposes a persisted commit index and does not claim its durability properties.
excluded: No multi-node cluster, partition, or crash of a leader is exercised, so the commit-loss consequence of a stale member set is not measured here.
No snapshot-on-start or FSM-implemented ConfigurationStore variant is exercised.
No production log store (for example a bolt-backed store) is exercised; the caller-side durability contract of CommitTrackingLogStore is assumed, not verified.

basis.prefix: Each case calls assuranceBuildPrefix: NewInmemTransport with a fresh random address; inmemConfig with LocalID = 'server-' + address and RestoreCommittedLogs = true; NewInmemCommitTrackingStore, NewInmemStore and NewInmemSnapshotStore; BootstrapCluster with a single Voter server at that address; NewRaft with a fresh MockFSM. The prefix then waits for real leadership through the normal election path, applies four LogCommand entries, and for the snapshot cases takes a real Snapshot, then issues AddNonvoter for a peer that never connects (committed by the single voter) and applies two more commands. GetCommitIndex, LastIndex and a per-index log scan record the persisted commit index and every configuration entry with its index and membership, then Shutdown closes the node. The case then creates a new transport bound to the same address, copies the config with RestoreCommittedLogs set to the case value, and calls NewRaft with the same log store, stable store, snapshot store and a fresh MockFSM. It polls State() every 5ms for 1500ms, then asks the main thread for the tracked configurations through r.configurationsCh (the same channel takeSnapshot uses) and reads snapshot index, AppliedIndex, CommitIndex and LastIndex.
basis.responsibility: raft's NewRaft is responsible for re-establishing the node's membership configuration from the node's own durable state before any election or quorum decision is made; the caller is responsible for supplying a log store whose GetCommitIndex is atomic with StoreLogs and for enabling RestoreCommittedLogs deliberately.

comparisons.description: A node restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs on top of stores whose log holds a committed configuration entry must still be able to elect a leader inside the observation window.
Control: the same prefix shape restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs off reaches leadership, which shows the nonprogress is specific to the replay path and not to the prefix.
The configuration recovered at startup must equal the newest configuration entry in the node's own log (index and voter/nonvoter membership).
Control: with the feature off the same predicate holds on the same prefix shape.
After restarting on a snapshot that predates a committed configuration change, the recovered configuration must include that committed entry.
Control: the same snapshot-plus-configuration prefix restarted with the feature off does recover the committed configuration entry.

scope.description: Build single-voter prefixes whose committed log lies about 9000 entries above an absent snapshot, then restart each prefix with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs on and off, calling NewRaft in a goroutine and reporting whether it returned within 8000ms together with a stack sample of the blocked goroutine.
assumptions: The prefix runs with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and a raised SnapshotThreshold so the commit index is staged into the commit-tracking log store and no automatic snapshot moves the replay bound.
The restarted node keeps the same address and ID as its prefix and uses a fresh in-memory MockFSM, so the whole committed log above the snapshot is replayed.
The observation window of 8000ms is used only to decide completion; the claim that the block persists comes from the source, since the channel's consumer is started only after the replay returns.
excluded: No lowered MaxAppendEntries case, so the proportional relation between the bound and MaxAppendEntries is source-derived and not measured.
No multi-node cluster, so member loss caused by a node that cannot start is not measured.
No production log store, and no store whose StageCommitIndex is atomic with StoreLogs.

basis.prefix: For each case, the harness builds its own prefix: NewInmemTransport with a random address, inmemConfig with LocalID = 'server-' + address, RestoreCommittedLogs true, SnapshotThreshold 1<<30 and SnapshotInterval one hour, plus NewInmemCommitTrackingStore, NewInmemStore and NewInmemSnapshotStore; BootstrapCluster with one Voter; NewRaft with a fresh MockFSM; wait for real leadership; then 9000 Apply calls, each waiting for its future. It records the store's commit index, last index, snapshot index and the computed batch count, then Shutdown. The case creates a new transport on the same address, copies the config with RestoreCommittedLogs set to the case value, and calls NewRaft in a separate goroutine. The main goroutine waits up to 8000ms for that call to return; if it does not, it samples all goroutine stacks with runtime.Stack and reports the excerpt around the first frame naming restoreFromCommittedLogs. If NewRaft returns, the harness waits up to one second for leadership, reports the state and then shuts the node down.
basis.responsibility: NewRaft owns completion of its own startup work, including the RestoreCommittedLogs replay it performs before returning; the caller cannot observe or interrupt a NewRaft call that has not returned, so any unbounded wait in that path is owned by the library.

comparisons.description: NewRaft must return for a node whose stores hold a committed log; a restart that replays more than the FSM channel can hold must not leave NewRaft waiting forever.
Control: the same prefix shape restarted with the replay disabled returns from NewRaft, which distinguishes the replay path from a property of the prefix.

scope.description: Restart single-voter prefixes with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and Config.MaxAppendEntries 16, once with a committed log of about 1500 entries (94 replay batches, below the 128-slot capacity) and once with about 3000 entries (188 batches, above it), calling NewRaft in a goroutine and reporting whether it returned within 8000ms plus a stack sample of the blocked goroutine. The same harness also reruns the two 9000-entry default-batch cases of the predecessor so the earlier observations stay in one artifact.
assumptions: MaxAppendEntries 16 is a legal configuration (ValidateConfig only requires a positive value) and is applied to both the prefix and the restart, so the batch size is the same on both sides of the comparison.
SnapshotThreshold is raised so no automatic snapshot moves the replay range, and the prefix runs with the feature enabled so the commit index is staged into the commit-tracking log store.
The 8000ms window decides completion only; the permanence of a block comes from the source, since the channel's consumer starts only after the blocked call returns.
excluded: No production log store, no multi-node cluster and no case in which an automatic snapshot overshoots the bound.

The below-bound case is not expected to elect a leader, because the configuration-recovery defect of the sibling investigation is active on the same restart; this experiment only asserts that NewRaft returns, and the leadership observation is reported without being asserted.

scope.description: Three in-memory voters A, B and C on one another's transports. A snapshots while {A,B,C} is committed; the leader then removes C, which commits against {A,B}, and commits three more entries. A is shut down and restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled over the same stores, while B is disconnected from A and C. The harness reports A's tracked configuration, whether A wins the election, and for a command applied after that: the client result, A's commit and applied index, whether A's FSM applied the payload, and whether the entry is present in A's, B's and C's logs.
assumptions: The removed server C keeps running and keeps answering AppendEntries, which is what a removal without shutting the process down leaves in place; the harness does not simulate C being killed.

A's snapshot is taken through the normal snapshot goroutine while the committed configuration is still {A,B,C}, so its configuration index is the bootstrap entry's index and its configuration contains C.
B is partitioned before A is restarted, so the committed configuration's only other voter cannot contribute an acknowledgement.
The nodes are in-memory transports and stores in one process; leadership, terms and quorum arithmetic are the real code paths.
excluded: No process-level restart, no production log store, and no attempt to complete the downstream loss of the entry; the predicate stops at the commitment rule.
No case in which the restarted node is the only stale voter or in which the stale configuration excludes a voter rather than including a removed one.

basis.prefix: The harness builds three assuranceMultiNode values: NewInmemTransport with a random address each, inmemConfig with LocalID = 'server-' + address and RestoreCommittedLogs true for every node, plus NewInmemCommitTrackingStore, NewInmemStore and NewInmemSnapshotStore per node. All transports are connected pairwise; BootstrapCluster is called on each node with the same three-voter configuration; NewRaft is called for each with a fresh MockFSM. The harness then waits for a real leader, applies one command through it, and takes a user snapshot on A through A.raft.Snapshot() while {A,B,C} is committed. It calls RemoveServer(C) on the leader and waits for that future, then applies three more commands, and records A's staged commit index, last index and the newest configuration entry in A's log. A is shut down and B is disconnected from A's transport and C's transport; a new transport bound to A's old address is created and connected to C only. NewRaft is called again on A's stores with RestoreCommittedLogs true and a fresh MockFSM. The harness reads A's tracked configurations through r.configurationsCh, waits up to five seconds for A to lead, and if it does, applies the payload 'stale-quorum-entry' with a two second timeout, then samples A's log entry term, the same index in B's and C's logs, A's commit and applied indexes, and A's FSM log contents.
basis.responsibility: raft's leader is responsible for committing an entry only when a majority of the configuration it is bound to has stored it, and raft's startup recovery is responsible for binding the leader to the configuration the committed log establishes rather than to an older one.

comparisons.description: Where the restart that tracks the snapshot's older three-voter configuration became leader while its log's committed configuration has two voters, committing an entry that its FSM applied and the client accepted while the committed configuration's other voter lacks it is a violation; such a witness shows the commit was decided by the removed server. Where A did not lead, the antecedent is false and nothing is claimed.

semantic_changes: Leadership is moved to A with LeadershipTransferToServer before the snapshot, because the election winner is arbitrary and removing the leader (ShutdownOnRemove defaults to true) would shut it down; the predecessor removed whichever node C was even when C led.

The pre-snapshot command is committed through A and the harness waits until A's FSM has applied a command entry, because runFSM refuses a snapshot request while its own last applied index is zero and a plain MockFSM never observes configuration or no-op entries.
Every node is shut down on all exit paths so no raft goroutine logs through the test logger after the test returns, which panicked the predecessor's later iterations.

A is then shut down and restarted again with the replay disabled, and the harness records the configuration the node comes up with.

The second restart uses the same stores with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs false and a fresh in-memory FSM, so the configuration can only come from the snapshot metadata and the log scan.
The flag-off restart is expected to run without a leader in the observation window because an empty configuration prevents the node from starting an election.

scope.description: Three in-memory voters A, B and C with Config.MaxAppendEntries 16 and no snapshots. A leader is chosen that is not A, about 3000 commands are committed so A's staged commit index sits about 3000 entries above its (absent) snapshot, and A is stopped. A is restarted over its own stores in a goroutine, in one case with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and in the other with it disabled, and the harness waits up to 8000ms for NewRaft to return. It then commits one command while two members are live, stops the member that is neither the leader nor A, and commits one further command, reporting the client results.
assumptions: The committed log above A's absent snapshot exceeds 128 * MaxAppendEntries (3000 entries against a 2048-entry bound), so the flag-on replay needs more batches than the FSM channel can hold.
The leader is moved away from A with the library's own leadership transfer so that stopping and restarting A does not remove the group's leader.
The member stopped after the restart is chosen to be the one that is neither the leader nor A, so the surviving live voters are the leader plus A when A started, and the leader alone when A did not.
The restart uses a fresh in-memory FSM and the same stores, transport address and ID as before.
excluded: No production store, no process-level restart and no disk fault: the blocked member's process is alive but its NewRaft call never returns.
No case in which the blocked member recovers later, and no measurement of how long a caller would wait before giving up on NewRaft.
Only one extra member is stopped, so the comparison is between a two-member and a one-member live group.

basis.prefix: The harness builds three assuranceMultiNode values with random in-memory transport addresses, inmemConfig overridden with MaxAppendEntries 16, SnapshotThreshold 1<<30, SnapshotInterval one hour and RestoreCommittedLogs true, plus a NewInmemCommitTrackingStore, NewInmemStore and NewInmemSnapshotStore per node. The transports are wired pairwise, BootstrapCluster is called on each node with the same three-voter configuration, and NewRaft is called with a fresh MockFSM each. basis.prefix: The harness builds three assuranceMultiNode values (random in-memory transport addresses, inmemConfig with RestoreCommittedLogs true, NewInmemCommitTrackingStore, NewInmemStore and NewInmemSnapshotStore per node), wires the transports pairwise, calls BootstrapCluster with the same three-voter configuration on each node and NewRaft with a fresh MockFSM each. It waits for a real leader, and if A won, moves leadership to B with LeadershipTransferToServer so that A can be restarted without stopping the cluster's leader. One command is committed and the harness waits until A's FSM has applied a command entry. A is shut down and a new transport on A's address is connected to B and C; NewRaft is called on A's stores with RestoreCommittedLogs true and a fresh MockFSM, and the harness records the tracked configurations through r.configurationsCh plus A's staged commit index, last index and newest configuration entry. One more command is committed and awaited in A's FSM, then A.Snapshot() is called and the harness reads the newest SnapshotMeta from A's snapshot store, comparing its Configuration and ConfigurationIndex with the log's configuration entry. A is shut down again, a further transport is created on the same address and connected to B and C, and NewRaft is called with RestoreCommittedLogs false; the harness records the restored snapshot index, the tracked configuration, the leader observation over 1500ms and the final state.
basis.responsibility: raft's snapshot writer is responsible for recording the committed configuration that the node's log establishes, and raft's startup recovery is responsible for establishing membership from durable state; a node that loses its configuration must not write that loss into the durable record other nodes and later restarts depend on.

comparisons.description: The configuration recorded in the snapshot metadata must be the configuration the node's own log establishes, not the empty configuration the recovery left behind.

A restart with the replay disabled must not come up without a membership configuration when its own snapshot and log establish one; a violating witness shows the loss is durable rather than confined to the replay path.

scope.description: Three in-memory voters A, B and C with Config.MaxAppendEntries 16 and no snapshots. A leader is chosen that is not A, about 3000 commands are committed so A's staged commit index sits about 3000 entries above its (absent) snapshot, and A is stopped. A is restarted over its own stores in a goroutine, in one case with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and in the other with it disabled, and the harness waits up to 8000ms for NewRaft to return. It then commits one command while two members are live, stops the member that is neither the leader nor A, and commits one further command, reporting the client results.
assumptions: The committed log above A's absent snapshot exceeds 128 * MaxAppendEntries (3000 entries against a 2048-entry bound), so the flag-on replay needs more batches than the FSM channel can hold.
The leader is moved away from A with the library's own leadership transfer so that stopping and restarting A does not remove the group's leader.
The member stopped after the restart is chosen to be the one that is neither the leader nor A, so the surviving live voters are the leader plus A when A started, and the leader alone when A did not.
The restart uses a fresh in-memory FSM and the same stores, transport address and ID as before.
excluded: No production store, no process-level restart and no disk fault: the blocked member's process is alive but its NewRaft call never returns.
No case in which the blocked member recovers later, and no measurement of how long a caller would wait before giving up on NewRaft.
Only one extra member is stopped, so the comparison is between a two-member and a one-member live group.

basis.prefix: The harness builds three assuranceMultiNode values with random in-memory transport addresses, inmemConfig overridden with MaxAppendEntries 16, SnapshotThreshold 1<<30, SnapshotInterval one hour and RestoreCommittedLogs true, plus a NewInmemCommitTrackingStore, NewInmemStore and NewInmemSnapshotStore per node. The transports are wired pairwise, BootstrapCluster is called on each node with the same three-voter configuration, and NewRaft is called with a fresh MockFSM each. The harness waits for a real leader and, if A won, transfers leadership to B with LeadershipTransferToServer before continuing. About 3000 commands are applied through the leader, each waiting for its future, and the harness records A's staged commit index, log last index, snapshot index and the implied replay batch count. A is shut down, a new transport bound to A's address is connected to B and C, and NewRaft is called in a separate goroutine on A's stores with a fresh MockFSM and the case's RestoreCommittedLogs value; the main goroutine waits up to 8000ms, and on non-return samples all goroutine stacks and reports the excerpt around the first frame naming restoreFromCommittedLogs. The harness then applies one command through the leader while two members are live, shuts down the member that is neither the leader nor A, applies one further command, and reports both results plus the state of the restart.
basis.responsibility: NewRaft owns completion of its own startup work, and a group's fault tolerance depends on every configured voter being able to run: a member that never finishes starting is a member the group does not have.

comparisons.description: Where the restarted member never returned from NewRaft, stopping one further member must not cost the group the ability to commit, because a member that could have started should still be available; the companion commit_while_two_live_ok field records that the group was committing before that stop.

Control: with the replay disabled the restarted member returns and the surviving pair still commits after one member is stopped, which attributes the loss in the companion comparison to the member that could not start.

scope.description: Two single-voter prefixes at Config.MaxAppendEntries 16 with no snapshot, built so that their persisted commit index ends at 2049 and 2050. Each prefix is restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, NewRaft is called in a goroutine, and the harness waits up to 8000ms. Both events report the entries in the replayed range and, separately, the number of entries in that range that become commit tuples and the batches those tuples need.
assumptions: The prefix applies commands one at a time and stops as soon as the store's commit index reaches the target, and the harness reports the value it actually reached.
The tuple count is derived by scanning the replayed range for LogCommand, LogBarrier and LogConfiguration entries, which is what prepareLog accepts at the default protocol version 3.
No snapshot exists on either prefix, so the replay starts at index 1 and the whole range is delivered.
The block is judged by non-return within 8000ms plus a stack sample naming the replay frames; permanence comes from the source, since the channel's only consumer starts after the replay returns.
excluded: No production store, no multi-node group and no default SnapshotThreshold: the point of this case is the boundary in batches, not the reachability of the range under default settings.
Only two points are placed, one batch below and one batch above the capacity, so no finer scan of the edge is attempted.

basis.prefix: For each target the harness creates an in-memory transport and a commit-tracking log store, configures inmemConfig with RestoreCommittedLogs true, MaxAppendEntries 16, SnapshotThreshold 1<<30 and SnapshotInterval one hour, calls BootstrapCluster with the single voter and NewRaft with a fresh MockFSM, waits for real leadership, and then applies one command at a time, re-reading the store's commit index after each apply, until it reaches the target. It records the commands applied, the log's last index, the staged commit index, the number of tuples in the replayed range, the batches those tuples need and the entry-based count, then shuts the prefix down. The restart creates a new transport on the same address, copies the config with RestoreCommittedLogs true, and calls NewRaft in a separate goroutine on the same stores with a fresh MockFSM; the main goroutine waits up to 8000ms and, on non-return, samples all goroutine stacks and reports the excerpt around the first frame naming restoreFromCommittedLogs.
basis.responsibility: NewRaft owns completion of its own startup work; the size of the replay it performs is set by the entries that become commit tuples, so the caller cannot infer the reachable replay from the log's index range alone.

comparisons.description: A replay of exactly 128 delivered batches fills the channel without exceeding it, so NewRaft must return.

A replay of 129 delivered batches needs one more batch than the channel holds, so NewRaft must still return; the pair with the 128-batch case places the bound at the channel's capacity in delivered batches rather than at a count of replayed log entries.

scope.description: Two single-voter prefixes built with DefaultConfig values left in place: SnapshotThreshold 8192, MaxAppendEntries 64, SnapshotInterval 120s, with only Config.RestoreCommittedLogs and the node timeouts changed. Each prefix applies 12000 commands, reports the committed range above its newest snapshot and whether that range exceeds the bound of 128*MaxAppendEntries, then restarts with the replay on in one case and off in the other, waiting up to 8000ms for NewRaft.
assumptions: The workload is a burst: the harness applies each command as fast as the in-memory stack allows, which is what a node whose write rate outpaces its snapshot cadence experiences.
The automatic snapshot loop wakes on a randomized timeout of up to SnapshotInterval, so the committed range above the newest snapshot can sit above the bound between checks.
The prefixes report whether any snapshot existed at restart, so the receipt shows whether the boundary condition held rather than assuming it.
The bound is the FSM channel's capacity of 128 batches times MaxAppendEntries commit tuples, which is what the earlier boundary experiment placed exactly.
excluded: No steady-state measurement of how long a node spends above the bound, and no production store, process-level restart or multi-node group.
No case in which an automatic snapshot fires during the burst; the receipt reports the snapshot index and the number of listed snapshots so a fired snapshot would be visible as a different setup.

basis.prefix: For each case the harness creates an in-memory transport, sets Config.LocalID and RestoreCommittedLogs true on inmemConfig (which overrides only the heartbeat, election, lease and commit timeouts), and leaves SnapshotThreshold, SnapshotInterval and MaxAppendEntries at their defaults. BootstrapCluster seeds the single voter and NewRaft starts the node with a fresh MockFSM; the harness waits for real leadership and then applies 12000 commands, each waiting for its future. It records the store's commit index, the log's last index, the last snapshot index, the number of snapshots listed, the three default parameters, the committed range above the snapshot and whether that range exceeds 128*MaxAppendEntries, then shuts the node down. The restart creates a new transport on the same address, copies the config with RestoreCommittedLogs set to the case value, and calls NewRaft in a separate goroutine on the same stores with a fresh MockFSM; the main goroutine waits up to 8000ms for it to return and, on non-return, samples all goroutine stacks and reports the excerpt around the first frame naming restoreFromCommittedLogs.
basis.responsibility: NewRaft owns completion of its own startup work, and the size of the replay it performs is set by how far the committed log has advanced beyond the newest snapshot; the library's default snapshot cadence is part of what determines that distance in normal operation.

comparisons.description: Where the committed range above the newest snapshot exceeds the bound with the library's default snapshot settings, a restart with the replay enabled must still return; the companion fields record the range, the bound and whether any snapshot existed.

Control: the same default configuration and the same committed range with the replay disabled returns from NewRaft, which attributes the non-return in the companion case to the replay rather than to the prefix.

scope.description: Three in-memory voters A, B and C. A leader is chosen, three commands are committed so A's staged commit index is non-zero, A is stopped and restarted over its own stores in one case with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and in the other with it disabled, and the harness records A's tracked configuration. The other two voters are then shut down, and the harness samples A's state every 5ms for 1500ms, reporting how often it was a follower, a candidate or a leader.
assumptions: The cluster configuration is stable, so no new configuration entry reaches A after its restart and its tracked configuration can only come from its own startup path.

A's stores hold no snapshot, so with the replay enabled the startup scan is skipped and A ends up with an empty tracked configuration; with the replay disabled the scan covers the log and A recovers the three-voter configuration.

Removing the other voters by shutting them down tests whether the surviving voter attempts candidacy, not whether it can win; with the recovered three-voter configuration A cannot win either, since its quorum is two.
The two cases use separate clusters built the same way, so the flag is the only difference.
excluded: No assertion about winning an election or about cluster availability; the observation is the candidate attempt itself.
No membership change after the restart, no partitioned-but-live peer, and no production store or process-level restart.

basis.prefix: For each case the harness builds three assuranceMultiNode values (random in-memory transport addresses, inmemConfig with RestoreCommittedLogs true and a fresh MockFSM per node), wires the transports pairwise, calls BootstrapCluster with the same three-voter configuration on each and NewRaft for each. It waits for a real leader and commits three commands through it, then records A's staged commit index and shuts A down. A new transport bound to A's address is connected to B and C, and NewRaft is called on A's stores with a fresh MockFSM and the case's RestoreCommittedLogs value; the harness reads A's tracked configurations through r.configurationsCh and reports the latest index, the voter count and the member ids. It then shuts B and C down, samples A's state every 5ms for 1500ms, and reports the follower, candidate and leader sample counts together with the last snapshot index and the final state.
basis.responsibility: raft's startup recovery is responsible for establishing the configuration the log already contains, and a voter's follower loop is responsible for attempting to acquire leadership when it stops hearing from a leader and its configuration allows it.

comparisons.description: A voter whose own log establishes the cluster configuration must attempt candidacy once it hears no leader and the other voters are gone; a violating witness shows a configured voter that can never become a candidate.

Control: the same node with the same log restarted with the replay disabled recovers its configuration and does attempt candidacy, which attributes the inertness in the companion case to the recovery path.
